messages.subject: Extracting derived variables in lavaan
parts:
I love the ability to use the := to calculate direct and indirect effects and their SEs.  One question, however. Is there a way to use inspect or some other function to extract these variables and their SE for use in other applications? For example, coef returns all model paths, but not paths defined by :=.  Similarly, I'm unclear as to how to extract their standard errors.

Thanks!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Extracting derived variables in lavaan
parts:
On 01/07/2016 07:00 PM, Jarrett Byrnes wrote:
> I love the ability to use the := to calculate direct and indirect
> effects and their SEs. One question, however. Is there a way to use
> inspect or some other function to extract these variables and their SE
> for use in other applications?

For the estimate alone, you can use coef() with the "all" option (see
below) (the documentation in class?lavaan still speaks of "user", which
still works, but 'all' is more natural)

But in general, I would use the parameterEstimates() function, which
just returns a data.frame, so you can easily 'select' the ':=' rows:

set.seed(1234)
X <- rnorm(100); M <- 0.5*X + rnorm(100)
Y <- 0.2*X + 0.8*M + rnorm(100)
Data <- data.frame(X,M,Y)

model <- ' M ~ a*X
Y ~ b*M + X
indirect := a*b
'
fit <- sem(model, data = Data)
summary(fit)

coef(fit, "all")
# a b Y~X M~~M Y~~Y X~~X indirect
# 0.474 0.888 0.236 1.054 0.898 0.999 0.421

PE <- parameterEstimates(fit)
PE[PE$op == ":=", c("est", "se")]

# est se
# 1 0.421 0.101

Yves.
